# Knosi — Full Project Context

> Long-form, AI-readable description of Knosi. This file is intended for
> large language models that need a single self-contained reference for
> what Knosi is, what it does, who it's for, and how it works.

Last updated: 2026-05-05.
Source of truth: https://github.com/zhousiyao03-cyber/knosi.
Hosted product: https://www.knosi.xyz.

---

## Elevator pitch

Knosi is a self-hostable, AI-native second brain. It captures the
high-signal answers you pull out of Claude or ChatGPT, turns them into
structured notes, indexes them with chunk-level hybrid retrieval, and
lets you ask AI on top of your own corpus instead of starting every
conversation from a blank context.

The hosted product runs at knosi.xyz. The same codebase is fully
self-hostable under AGPL-3.0 — Docker Compose, single-VPS Hetzner
deployment, and k3s setups are all documented in the repository.
Self-hosted instances get every feature for free; the hosted Pro tier
exists to fund development, not to gate functionality.

## Who Knosi is for

- Developers and AI-heavy knowledge workers who treat Claude / ChatGPT
  as a daily research tool and want their good answers to survive past
  the chat window.
- Independent builders running their own infrastructure who want a
  Notion-shaped knowledge base they can fully own.
- Engineers studying for new domains (AI engineering, backend
  architecture) who want a structured curriculum view of what they
  already know vs. what is still a blank spot.
- Anyone with a Claude Pro / Max subscription who would rather route
  their AI queries through an existing flat-rate plan than burn extra
  per-token API credits.

If you only need a plain note-taking app, Notion or Obsidian will serve
you well. Knosi is differentiated by being designed around the
"AI conversation → permanent knowledge" loop as a first-class workflow.

## What's distinctive

1. **Hybrid RAG by default.** Semantic retrieval, BM25-style keyword
   recall, and adjacent-paragraph expansion all run together; results
   come back with clickable source citations to the originating note.
   When no embedding provider is configured the system still works
   — it falls back to keyword-only retrieval.

2. **Bring-your-own-Claude.** The Claude Code Daemon routes Ask AI
   through your local Claude CLI session, so a Claude Pro / Max
   subscription replaces the need for a separate API budget. The
   daemon supports both local dev and remote self-hosted deployments,
   with Redis-backed live token fan-out and Redis/SSE wakeups so it
   doesn't have to idle-poll.

3. **Capture from Claude Web and Claude Code.** A remote MCP endpoint
   lets Claude Web connect via OAuth and write into a `knowledge:write_inbox`
   scope. The Knosi CLI plus a Claude Code skill template lets you
   save explicit conversation excerpts from a local Claude Code
   session. Both flows land raw captures in an `AI Inbox` folder.

4. **Per-user provider config.** AI providers are not configured in
   environment variables — they are added per-user in `/settings`.
   You can mix providers across roles (Chat / Task / Embedding), so
   a typical setup might be DeepSeek for chat, GPT-4o-mini for
   structured tasks, and OpenAI text-embedding-3-small for embeddings.

5. **Self-hosted parity.** Every feature in the hosted product is
   available under AGPL-3.0 self-host. There is no "open core" gating.

## Active modules (May 2026)

The single source of truth for the active sidebar layout is
`src/components/layout/navigation.ts`. As of this writing, the live
groups and modules are:

- **CAPTURE**
  - `/dashboard` — Home (today's focus, 30-day heatmap, recent notes)
  - `/notes` — Notion-style note workspace
  - `/ask` — Ask AI over your corpus (hybrid RAG)
  - `/council` — Multi-perspective AI council prompt UI
- **LEARN**
  - `/learn` — Topic-oriented learning notebooks
  - `/learn/map` — Curriculum map (knowledge gap analysis)
  - `/projects` — OSS project notes / discovery
  - `/speak` — Shadow-drill English fluency module
  - `/words` — Per-word pronunciation drill
- **TRACK**
  - `/portfolio` — Portfolio tracker (positions, AI analysis, news)
  - `/focus` — Focus Tracker dashboard (paired with desktop collector)
- **INSIGHTS**
  - `/usage` — Token usage dashboard
  - `/preferences` — User preferences
- **REST**
  - `/drifter` — Quiet, low-stakes browsing surface

Optional modules (Token Usage, Portfolio, OSS Projects, Focus Tracker)
are gated behind environment flags in self-hosted deployments — set
both the server-side and `NEXT_PUBLIC_` flag to `true` to surface them.

## Feature inventory

### Core Knowledge

- **Rich text editor.** Notion-style block editor on Tiptap v3.
  Includes code blocks with language selector, Mermaid diagrams (with
  `securityLevel: "strict"` for XSS hardening), Excalidraw whiteboards,
  callouts, toggles, tables with toolbar, side-by-side image rows,
  TOC block with collapsible sidebar, drag-and-drop block sorting,
  slash commands, search-and-replace, and mixed Markdown paste.
- **Notes.** Full-width cover images, type and tag metadata, hover-
  to-insert controls, block-level move/copy/delete/transform, auto-
  save with loss prevention, public read-only sharing links, and a
  one-click daily journal that inherits from a plan template.
- **Learning notebooks.** Topic-oriented study sessions with AI-
  generated outlines, blind-spot analysis, review-question generation,
  and Ask AI scoped to the topic's note context.
- **Curriculum map.** A `/learn/map` view of knowledge gaps across
  target roles (currently AI Engineer and Backend Architect) with
  ~240 seeded topics. Each topic has a 4-state mastery toggle:
  blank, heard, learning, mastered. Auto-links existing notes by
  string matching; click a topic to open a side panel with the
  mastery toggle, linked notes, and a quick "Create new note"
  action that pre-fills curriculum tags. The note editor surfaces
  curriculum tags inline so you can see how a note maps back into
  the curriculum.
- **OSS project notes.** Per-project note collections with repo
  metadata, tag filtering, per-note read-only links, and long-term
  analysis archiving.

### AI

- **Ask AI.** Chunk-level hybrid RAG with semantic retrieval, keyword
  recall, adjacent-paragraph expansion, and clickable source
  citations. Falls back to keyword-only when no embedding provider
  is configured.
- **Claude Code Daemon.** Routes Ask AI through your local Claude
  Pro / Max subscription via the Knosi CLI. No extra API spend.
  Works against both local dev and the self-hosted web deployment,
  with Redis-backed live token fan-out plus Redis/SSE wakeups so
  the daemon does not have to idle-poll claims.
- **Structured AI calls.** Learning outline generation, OSS analysis,
  and portfolio news summarization all run through the configured
  provider independently of the chat daemon.
- **Claude capture integrations.**
  - Claude Web → remote MCP endpoint (`/api/mcp` + OAuth at
    `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`). Adds Knosi as a
    custom connector in Claude Web. Scopes: `knowledge:read`,
    `knowledge:write_inbox`. Captures land in `AI Inbox`.
  - Claude Code → Knosi CLI + personal skill at
    `~/.claude/skills/save-to-knosi/SKILL.md`. Save explicit
    conversation excerpts into `AI Inbox` from inside Claude Code.

### Developer Workflow

- **Token usage dashboard.** Auto-reads local Claude Code session
  files (`~/.claude/projects/`) and Codex state databases
  (`~/.codex/state*.sqlite`). Aggregates across all workspaces and
  subagents. Manual entry is supported for OpenAI API and other
  off-disk sources.
- **Focus tracker.** Server-side ingestion plus a `/focus` web UI
  for app-level time tracking. Pairs with a desktop Tauri collector
  (focus-tracker repository) — there is a macOS DMG download for
  Apple Silicon. Sign in with the same Knosi account used in the web app.
- **Installable PWA.** Standalone web app manifest with dedicated
  192×192, 512×512, and Apple touch icons that work on the self-
  hosted Hetzner deployment.

### Optional Modules

- **Portfolio tracker.** Position management with Yahoo Finance and
  CoinGecko real-time prices, AI position analysis, and news
  aggregation via Marketaux or Google News RSS. Server-side cron
  jobs auto-refresh prices and news.
- **Speak.** Shadow-drill module at `/speak`. One native English
  sentence at a time, browser TTS plays it, you shadow it, press
  Next. Per-sentence lifetime practice count synced across devices.
  Ships with 30 hand-picked working-professional sentences.
- **Words.** Per-word pronunciation drill at `/words`. Each card
  shows stress visualization, IPA, brief Chinese meaning, and a
  native example sentence. 100 hand-picked seeds. Add your own
  words; AI enriches them on save. Browser TTS reused from `/speak`.
- **Search.** `Cmd+K` global note search with keyword highlighting.
- **Dark mode.** Global toggle, full dark mode coverage.

## Hosted vs self-hosted

Knosi is AGPL-3.0 and fully self-hostable for free.

The hosted product at knosi.xyz offers a paid Pro tier
($9 / month or $90 / year) with included Knosi AI (no API key
needed), 80 Ask AI calls per day, unlimited notes, 10 GB image
storage, and access to the Portfolio, Focus, OSS Projects, and
Claude Capture modules. See https://www.knosi.xyz/pricing for the
full plan comparison.

Self-hosted deployments are unaffected — every feature stays free.

## Tech stack

| Layer            | Technology                                  |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Framework        | Next.js 16 (App Router) + React 19          |
| Styling          | Tailwind CSS v4                             |
| API              | tRPC v11 + Zod v4                           |
| Database         | Drizzle ORM + SQLite via libsql / Turso     |
| Auth             | Auth.js v5 (GitHub / Google + email/password)|
| AI orchestration | Vercel AI SDK v6                            |
| Vector search    | Milvus (production) + in-memory fallback    |
| Object storage   | S3-compatible (R2 / MinIO / S3)             |
| Editor           | Tiptap v3 (ProseMirror)                     |
| Diagrams         | Mermaid + Excalidraw                        |
| Content fetch    | @mozilla/readability + linkedom             |
| Testing          | Playwright (E2E)                            |
| Deployment       | Docker Compose / Hetzner-style self-hosting |

## High-level architecture

- **Edge layer.** Caddy reverse proxy on the production server,
  Cloudflare in front for DNS / DDoS / analytics. The hosted product
  uses a single Hetzner Ubuntu host running Docker Compose; the same
  stack ships in `docker-compose.prod.yml`.
- **App.** Next.js 16 App Router. The authenticated route group is
  `src/app/(app)/`; each subdirectory is a sidebar module.
- **API.** tRPC v11 with Zod v4. Each module has its own router
  under `src/server/routers/`, mounted into the root `_app.ts`.
- **Database.** Drizzle ORM on libsql (SQLite-compatible). Local dev
  uses a file-backed database under `data/`; production uses Turso.
  Migrations live in `drizzle/`.
- **AI.** All AI plumbing lives under `src/server/ai/`:
  - `agentic-rag.ts` — top-level retrieval pipeline
  - `chat-prepare.ts` + `chat-system-prompt.ts` — chat orchestration
  - `chunker.ts` + `indexer.ts` — note chunking and indexing
  - `reranker.ts` — cross-encoder reranking on top of recall
  - `embeddings.ts` — provider-agnostic embedding adapter
  - `provider/*.ts` — OpenAI-compatible / Local / Daemon adapters
  - `tools/*.ts` — tool-use definitions for the chat agent
- **Capture surfaces.**
  - `/api/mcp` exposes a remote MCP endpoint for Claude Web.
  - The Knosi CLI (npm: `@knosi/cli`) handles auth, daemon mode,
    save-to-knosi flows, and skill installation.
- **Background jobs.** Cron entries on the host server kick a
  protected `/api/jobs/tick` endpoint to drive scheduled work
  (price refresh, news aggregation, indexer catch-up).

The repository's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md describe the working
agreement — they are useful context for anyone modifying the code.

## Quick start

### Docker (recommended)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zhousiyao03-cyber/knosi.git
cd knosi
docker compose up -d
# → http://localhost:3000
```

### Local development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zhousiyao03-cyber/knosi.git
cd knosi
pnpm install
cp .env.example .env.local
pnpm db:push
pnpm dev
# → http://localhost:3200
```

In development mode a test account is auto-provisioned:
`test@secondbrain.local` / `test123456`. It is only created
when `NODE_ENV=development`.

### Hetzner single-server deploy

The repo includes a production Docker Compose stack:
- `docker-compose.prod.yml` — app + Redis + Caddy
- `ops/hetzner/Caddyfile` — HTTPS reverse proxy
- `ops/hetzner/bootstrap.sh` — swap, Docker, firewall, `/srv/knosi`
- `ops/hetzner/deploy.sh` — server-side deployment entrypoint
- `.github/workflows/deploy-hetzner.yml` — push-to-main auto deploy

Push to `main` triggers a GitHub Action that lints, rsyncs the
repository to the server, runs `ops/hetzner/deploy.sh`, rebuilds
the image, performs a rolling restart, and waits for the health
check on `http://127.0.0.1:3000/login`.

## Configuration overview

### Required

```bash
TURSO_DATABASE_URL=file:data/second-brain.db   # or libsql://... in prod
AUTH_SECRET=<openssl rand -base64 32>
KNOSI_SECRET_KEY=<openssl rand -hex 32>        # encrypts stored API keys
```

Without `KNOSI_SECRET_KEY` the server refuses to start.

### Auth providers

```bash
AUTH_GITHUB_ID=...
AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET=...
AUTH_GOOGLE_ID=...
AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET=...
AUTH_URL=https://knosi.example.com   # required in prod for OAuth callbacks
AUTH_TRUST_HOST=true
```

### Object storage (image uploads)

```bash
S3_ENDPOINT=https://s3.example.com
S3_REGION=auto
S3_BUCKET=knosi-assets
S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://assets.example.com
```

### Feature flags

| Module                  | Server flag             | Client flag                          |
|-------------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Token Usage Dashboard   | `ENABLE_TOKEN_USAGE`    | `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_TOKEN_USAGE`     |
| Portfolio Tracker       | `ENABLE_PORTFOLIO`      | `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_PORTFOLIO`       |
| OSS Project Notes       | `ENABLE_OSS_PROJECTS`   | `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_OSS_PROJECTS`    |
| Focus Tracker           | `ENABLE_FOCUS_TRACKER`  | `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_FOCUS_TRACKER`   |

### AI rate limit

```bash
AI_DAILY_LIMIT=50   # per-user daily cap; 0 = unlimited
```

## AI provider configuration

AI providers are configured per user in `/settings`, not via env vars.
Sign in, click "+ Add provider", and pick one of:

- **OpenAI-compatible API.** OpenAI, DeepSeek, Moonshot, SiliconFlow,
  Groq, or any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Provide the base
  URL, API key, and a label.
- **Local model.** Ollama / LM Studio / any OpenAI-compatible local
  server (defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` for Ollama).
- **Claude Code Daemon.** Routes Ask AI through your local Claude
  Pro / Max subscription via the Knosi CLI daemon. No API key
  required.
- **Transformers.js.** In-process embedding-only kind for the RAG
  indexer when you don't want to call out at all.

After adding providers, assign one to each AI Role
(Chat / Task / Embedding) on the same Settings page. Roles can use
different providers and models — a typical setup is DeepSeek for
chat, GPT-4o-mini for structured tasks, OpenAI
`text-embedding-3-small` for embeddings.

## Claude Code Daemon

To route Ask AI through your local Claude subscription:

```bash
# global, against the hosted product
npx @knosi/cli --url https://www.knosi.xyz

# during local dev
pnpm daemon
```

Requirements: Claude CLI installed and logged in (`claude login`).
The daemon opens a notification stream for queued AI tasks, executes
them via your local Claude CLI, and streams results back.

## Claude Web connector (MCP)

Knosi exposes a remote MCP surface for Claude Web. The connector
points to:

```
/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
/api/mcp
```

In Claude Web, add a custom connector that points at your Knosi
deployment. The OAuth flow uses your existing Knosi account and
grants scoped access for `knowledge:read` and
`knowledge:write_inbox`. Saved conversations land in the root-level
`AI Inbox` folder as raw captures.

## Save-to-Knosi from Claude Code

```bash
# 1. Log the CLI into your Knosi deployment
npx @knosi/cli auth login https://www.knosi.xyz

# 2. Install the personal Claude Code skill
npx @knosi/cli install-skill

# 3. Save a raw conversation payload
cat payload.json | npx @knosi/cli save-ai-note --json
```

The installed skill template is written to
`~/.claude/skills/save-to-knosi/SKILL.md` and is intended for
explicit user-triggered saves only.

## Project structure

```
src/
  app/                Next.js App Router pages and API routes
    (app)/            Authenticated route group (each dir = sidebar module)
    api/              tRPC and webhook endpoints
    layout.tsx        Root layout, metadata, JSON-LD
    page.tsx          Public landing
    sitemap.ts        Sitemap (public pages only — share/* excluded)
    robots.ts         AI-aware robots policy
  components/
    editor/           Tiptap editor: extensions, blocks, toolbar, paste
    layout/           Sidebar, navigation, mobile nav
    marketing/        Landing page + landing data (FAQ, links)
    ui/               Shared UI primitives (toast, search dialog, ...)
  server/
    db/               Drizzle schema + libsql connection
    routers/          tRPC routers (one file per module)
    ai/               RAG pipeline, chunker, indexer, reranker,
                      provider abstraction, agent tools
    focus/            Focus tracker interval slicing + aggregation
  lib/                Client utilities, tRPC client, note templates
e2e/                  Playwright E2E tests
eval/                 RAG and agent eval datasets + run results
ops/                  Deployment scripts (Hetzner k3s, Turso rollout)
drizzle/              Auto-generated migrations
docs/changelog/       Per-task change log
docs/superpowers/     Design specs (`specs/`) and historical plans
public/               Static assets, including this file
```

## Privacy and security posture

- Auth-gated routes are explicitly disallowed in `robots.txt` and
  return `noindex` headers as a belt-and-suspenders measure.
- `/share/<token>` is a private capability URL. Share tokens are
  never enumerated in the sitemap — listing them there would turn
  "anyone with the link" into "indexed by search engines and
  scrapable forever". Each share page also returns
  `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` for engines that ignore
  robots.txt on already-known URLs.
- Stored API keys are encrypted at rest with `KNOSI_SECRET_KEY`;
  losing the key forces every user to re-enter their provider
  credentials but does not allow plaintext recovery.
- Mermaid is configured with `securityLevel: "strict"` to prevent
  XSS via diagram syntax.
- The hosted product enforces a per-user daily Ask AI rate limit
  via `AI_DAILY_LIMIT`.

## AI crawler policy

The site `robots.txt` at https://www.knosi.xyz/robots.txt is
classified by crawler intent, not a single allow/deny:

- **Allow** — search and retrieval bots (`OAI-SearchBot`,
  `Claude-SearchBot`, `PerplexityBot`) and user-triggered fetchers
  (`ChatGPT-User`, `Claude-User`, `Google-Agent`, `Perplexity-User`).
  These return real-time citations to users; we want to be
  discoverable and accurately quoted.
- **Block** — training-only crawlers (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`,
  `Meta-ExternalAgent`, `CCBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `cohere-ai`,
  `FacebookBot`, `Amazonbot`) plus opt-out tokens
  (`Google-Extended`, `Applebot-Extended`) and known undeclared /
  non-compliant scrapers (`Bytespider`, `ImagesiftBot`, `Diffbot`).
- **Default `*`** — same policy as classic search bots: allow public
  pages, disallow private/auth-gated routes.

This signals: cite us in answers, but please don't ingest us into
training corpora.

## Frequently asked

**What is Knosi?**
Knosi is a self-hostable, AI-native second brain for developers.
It turns Claude / ChatGPT outputs into searchable, reusable
knowledge.

**Is Knosi just a note-taking app?**
No. It is designed around the AI workflow first — note-taking,
retrieval, and AI-powered querying are unified so the output of
your AI sessions becomes long-term knowledge instead of disposable
chat history.

**Why not just use Notion or Obsidian?**
Those tools are great, but they are not built around capturing and
reusing AI output as a first-class workflow. Knosi is.

**Do I need an API key?**
Not on the hosted version. On a self-hosted instance you bring
your own provider — OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, a local model,
or the Claude Code Daemon if you already pay for Claude Pro / Max.

**Can I self-host it?**
Yes. Knosi runs anywhere Node.js and SQLite run — Docker, k3s,
a single VPS, or your laptop. The repository includes the full
deploy setup used by knosi.xyz (Caddy + Docker on Hetzner) as a
reference.

**Who is it for?**
Developers, AI-heavy knowledge workers, independent builders, and
anyone who wants AI outputs to become reusable knowledge instead
of disposable chat history.
